links.outcome: LLM accuracy on medical benchmarks with and without multiple-choice answer options
links.effect: Mean accuracy fell from 82.3% to 50.9% when answer choices were withheld. The strongest models exceed the human-expert baseline in standard multiple choice. Smaller models trail larger ones by 8.7 percentage points.
links.quote: Withholding the answer choices, however, makes every model struggle: mean accuracy falls from 82.3% to 50.9%, and the two largest drops belong to the medically specialised models.

unlisted_practices: Testing benchmark contamination and memorization by reconstructing hidden questions from answer choices
Weighing accuracy against inference cost when choosing models
Ensembling several models to improve medical question answering

screen.reason: Evaluates medical LLM capabilities, memorization/benchmark contamination, and ensembling across multiple-choice medical benchmark datasets.
